title: How the Hoover Dam was built

lines.text: This is how they built the Hoover Dam, a wall holding back an entire lake.
First, crews dug four giant tunnels through the canyon walls.
The river was pushed into them, leaving the riverbed dry.
Holes drilled in the bedrock were filled with grout, to stop water sneaking underneath.
Then concrete rose as over two hundred blocks, five feet at a time.
Poured at once, it would have taken about a hundred twenty five years to cool.
So cold water ran through hundreds of miles of pipe inside.
Next, the tunnels closed, and Lake Mead filled up.
It's six hundred sixty feet thick at the base, because water pressure grows with depth.
Its weight and curved arch shape hold the lake back.
Towers feed water down to seventeen turbines that make electricity.
Spillways let floods escape around the sides.
Would you trust a wall holding back a lake?
